findings.text: Provides cached directory child lookup that samples the rename sequence lock, probes the hash, and repeats while a concurrent rename invalidates the snapshot, returning a referenced entry on hit or null on miss.

Mount write access follows strict pairing where acquisition starts filesystem write protection before taking mount write count and release drops mount count before ending filesystem protection; open and truncate paths hold it only across mutation windows.

Slow create or open holds the parent directory inode lock for the whole lookup plus optional creation sequence, using exclusive mode when creation was requested or a creation error was recorded and shared mode otherwise, and refuses dead directories early.

Slow open validates or allocates a dentry, revalidates cached entries with invalidation fallback, delegates to filesystem atomic open when present, otherwise performs filesystem lookup completion, then either returns positive or non-create results or proceeds to creation; a delegation break on the parent causes wait and full retry.

Final open step merges intent flags, dispatches dot forms through dedicated handling, tries fast lookup that may run in RCU mode, exits RCU before slow lookup, treats already opened or created results as terminal by installing the new dentry, and otherwise steps into the found dentry while clearing open intent flags on trailing failure.

Fast open rejects creation with trailing slash as directory error, skips cache work for exclusive creation, forces follow plus directory semantics when trailing slash remains, and discards negative cache hits for creation because creation requires the directory lock.

Creation permission is a conjunction of path mknod authorization, filesystem idmap ownership, directory write plus execute permission, and inode creation authorization, evaluated in that order with first failure returned.

Atomic open marks the file path with a sentinel, invokes the filesystem method with namei-normalized flags, finalizes lookup state, then accepts either an opened file with possible dentry replacement or a no-open result with possible replacement while treating negative residue as missing; unset path or filesystem error produces an I/O or mapped creation error.
Open flag normalization maps the combined read-write access encoding to the internal representation expected by name resolution by decrementing only that encoding.

Creation notification first records an audit child event then emits a directory entry event; name notification is skipped entirely when the superblock has no watchers and otherwise forwards mask, dentry, parent and name with zero cookie.

Open completion finalizes RCU and scoped walks unless already opened or created, audits existing objects, enforces exclusion against non-created results, rejects directories for creation, applies sticky-directory protection and type checks, suppresses access and truncate work for new files, and otherwise sequences access check, filesystem open, post-open authorization and optional truncate under mount write hold.

Walk completion exits RCU mode with root handling for non-preset non-scoped cases, rejects scoped resolutions whose final path escapes the root, and only for jumped paths with weak revalidation support invokes the dentry method, mapping non-positive outcomes to stale or returned errors.
Path containment test acquires mount read protection and climbs mount parents through mountpoints until reaching the root mount, then checks mount identity and directory ancestry.

Sticky directory creation allows non-sticky parents, unprotected regular files or FIFOs when corresponding controls are disabled, owner match on directory versus object, or current filesystem identity match; world-writable sticky parents deny with audit, while group-writable parents deny only selected FIFO or regular types at higher protection levels.

Truncate handling takes inode write access, authorizes truncation, delegates to attribute change for zero length with time and open markers, and releases access; the attribute path rejects negative lengths, attaches the file when present, strips privileges with forced update, and serializes the change under a killable directory inode lock.
Killable inode acquisition takes the inode semaphore in write mode and propagates interruption instead of blocking uninterruptibly.

Absolute resolution initializes state, optionally steps down into the starting point, iterates path walk plus trailing component handling until stable, handles mountpoint descent with suppression of later weak revalidation, completes RCU and scope checks, enforces directory expectation, and on success transfers path ownership to the caller before terminating the walk.

Trailing component handling upgrades to follow plus directory semantics when the final name has leftover characters; downward traversal pins the current dentry outside RCU mode, preserves sequence state, and enters the same dentry without following.

Temporary file creation resolves the parent as a directory, holds mount write across filesystem temporary creation, audits the resulting anonymous file and releases all references; O-path opening resolves the target, audits it, opens it through the filesystem and then releases the path.

Write access denial uses a single atomic decrement that succeeds only while the inode writer count stays positive, yielding text-busy on executables under concurrent write; executable denial is bypassed for hierarchical storage manager notification modes.

Loader release drops the saved executable file without freeing the pointer wrapper, while close during exec restores write access and releases the reference; format assignment swaps the memory descriptor format with balanced module reference handling for old and new values.

In-memory ELF note descriptor holds a name pointer, integer type, payload length and payload pointer; serialized footprint is the fixed note header plus name with terminator and payload each rounded up to four-byte alignment.

Note serialization builds a header with name length including terminator, payload length and type, then emits header, name, padding, payload and trailing padding as one chained operation that fails if any emission fails.

Core dump emission first drains any pending skip bytes once, then appends bytes only while total stays within limit and no fatal signal or freeze is pending, advancing file offset and both written and logical position counters on success and reporting failure without partial accounting otherwise.
Kernel internal write wraps a single in-kernel vector bounded by the maximum I/O count, initializes a source iterator over it, and forwards to the iterator write path at the supplied offset.
On this configuration architecture mmap randomization is zero and randomization of the break address leaves it unchanged.
ELF readable mapping does not imply executable permission regardless of stack markings on this configuration.

Secondary personality selection delegates to primary personality handling, thread start forwards executable, registers, entry and stack to low-level start, and additional page setup forwards binprm and interpreter to architecture setup.

Delegation presence either reflects a stored inode pointer with wait implemented as break plus iput and clear, or is hard-wired absent with wait treated as unreachable; callers must only wait after presence was reported and must retry the enclosing open when wait succeeds.
Regular-file testing compares the cached entry type against the regular value, and backing inode access returns the dentry inode directly on this configuration.
Public truncate entry validates length and serializes size change with privilege handling, while public dump emission exposes skip-aware bounded output for core files.

Remaining in RCU mode across slow open without successful transition requests caller retry, exclusive creation against an existing object reports existence, creation against a directory or truncation of non-regular objects is rejected, and positive internal status from post-open handling is escalated to invalid argument.
